runtime.shapingRequirement: HarfBuzz WASM (harfbuzzjs) over the pinned font bytes, opened by file name from import.meta.url and hashed into fontSha256Measured
runtime.shapingRequirementNote: D-019 removed Pango, FreeType, Fribidi and fontconfig from the path. sharp paints a path-only SVG that carries no <text> element and no family name, so no renderer can substitute a face.
runtime.rasterRequirement: sharp 0.34.5 for painting the path-only SVG and encoding the PNG
runtime.ringCarrierRule: D-020: the jump-ring carrier is the largest contour of the outermost non-mark base glyph at each end, read from the font outlines and GDEF classes before rasterisation. Each carrier offers a ladder of anchors - the columns of its load-bearing metal, from the outer edge of the stroke inward - and the two sides are scored together, so the piece hangs level and neither end is cantilevered. ringPlacement is welded or none; a name that cannot seat two rings under the gates raises identity_no_ring_seat and is routed to operator review before any spend.
runtime.ringCarrierGdefNote: GDEF class 3 is the font's own answer only where the face carries it: measured over the 48-name matrix, NotoNaskhArabic and NotoKufiArabic class 85 of 286 shaped glyphs as marks. cairo (the Latin face of kufi) classifies nothing at all (class 0 for all 259), rakkas returns class 3 for none of 196 and ScheherazadeNew for only 7 of 207 because both draw the nuqta inside the base contour, and PlayfairDisplay shapes no separate mark at all. On those faces the exclusion is geometry: the carrier is the largest contour of the glyph, which a dot never is, and the contour-area and height fractions hold out a glyph whose largest contour is not letter-like. The smallest height fraction a real letter body reached across all six faces is 0.435 (PlayfairDisplay), so the glyph-relative floor moved from 0.4 to 0.3 in fix pass 5; the tallest dot contour measured where a dot is its own contour is 0.129 (cairo).
runtime.ringWeldRule: A weld fillet may only cover metal of the carrier contour it is welding to. Any other contour's pre-ring ink under the fillet counts as welded and refuses the piece (identity_ring_welded_to_glyph). Measured on the decoded PNG, the two ring holes must also sit at least IDENTITY_RING_MIN_SPAN_FRACTION of the finished ink width apart (identity_ring_span_too_narrow, IDENTITY_RING_SHARED_GLYPH_MIN_SPAN_FRACTION for a one-letter name), no more than IDENTITY_RING_MAX_TILT_DEGREES off horizontal (identity_ring_tilt_too_steep) and with no more than IDENTITY_RING_MAX_OVERHANG_FRACTION of the name's own ink outside the nearer hole on either side (identity_ring_overhang_too_wide; the ruler is the name's ink box before any ring, so ring metal is in neither the numerator nor the denominator). A ring is welded at the shoulder of its letter: the anchor ladder is cut to the top IDENTITY_RING_ANCHOR_MAX_DEPTH_FRACTION of the carrier contour's own height, and the post between the anchor and the centre of the hole may not exceed the smaller of IDENTITY_RING_MAX_POST_FRACTION of the name's ink height and IDENTITY_RING_MAX_POST_PX (identity_ring_post_too_long). No enclosed region of a few pixels may survive into the encoded bytes (identity_stencil_pinhole); a counter that the construction squeezed under that floor is never filled to hide it.
runtime.constructionGeometryRule: P2-2b (D-021): the stencil is the whole physical piece. solveIdentity takes the approved pendant construction and draws the structure it carries: framed-minimal is a rectangular frame with softly rounded corners around the name, welded into the bottom rail at two points, with the two rings on the top rail near its corners; diamond-rails is one straight rail above the name and one below, each welded to the name at two points, with the two rings at the outer ends of the top rail. classical and origami-ribbon are the lettering alone, and the ribbon's folded facets are a finish the stencil never claims. Rail thickness, inset, corner radius, rail gap, overhang and ring end inset are engine constants in shaping.ts, drawn with the same capsule primitive as the bridges. The name is resampled to make room (carrier.nameScale) and refused with identity_carrier_no_room below IDENTITY_CARRIER_MIN_NAME_SCALE; the structure may only add metal (identity_carrier_moved_ink). ringPlacement is welded, frame or none and carrier.kind is the detail; the construction id is a fingerprint input, so the same name in two constructions is two artifacts.

fonts.note: Replaces Amiri for classic on 2026-08-27: Amiri stacks lam-ya in HarfBuzz; approved renders were flat.

Live since P1-3: Noto Kufi Arabic has no Latin coverage at all, so the English side of the kufi family renders on Cairo, the geometric sans from the same licensed pack. LIVE_STYLES in caleums-arabic-v3.ts pins this sha.
Retired 2026-08-27: the cursive stencil was unreproducible by the image model and misread by the name reader; replaced by Playfair Display.
Latin name stencil face pinned 2026-08-27, replacing Great Vibes: a clean serif rendered at weight 700 with -0.04em tracking so the glyphs fuse into one pendant body.

approvalRules.liveStylesNote: All six ship since 2026-08-27; LIVE_IDENTITY_STYLES in caleums-arabic-v3.ts is the source of truth and this list mirrors it. classic, diwani and signature share the Naskh face by design (identity package review finding 4, accepted risk); DS-4 limits what the shop sells to what phase 3 proves.

engineReleaseNote: D-019 renamed the release from caleums-arabic-v3 because one solver now serves both scripts. The directory keeps the old name so no font file has to move; CALEUMS_IDENTITY_FONT_DIRECTORY in shaping.ts repeats it as a literal.
